agent.leadHtml: In the Netherlands this role has a name: aanhuurmakelaar, an agent hired by the tenant and paid only by the tenant. We don't list apartments, we don't represent landlords, and we don't take a cent from the other side of the table. We find, we apply, we negotiate, and we read the contract before you sign it.
legalHtml: We work exclusively for you. BOOM Amsterdam never accepts fees, commissions or referrals from landlords, their agents, or listing platforms. Dutch law forbids an agent from charging both sides of a rental, and we agree with it: an agent paid by the landlord cannot negotiate your rent down.

You pay for the work, not the outcome of a game we rigged. Our fee covers search, dossier, applications, viewings and contract review. Your €99 founding deposit is refundable before work starts and is deducted from your service fee.

how.h2: Five steps. One person. Your phone.

steps.title: Brief
steps.text: A 20-minute call. Budget, move-in date, neighbourhoods, who's moving, and what your income situation looks like on paper. We tell you honestly what your budget buys in Amsterdam today.

steps.title: Dossier, in 24 hours
steps.text: Your application pack in the format Dutch landlords and agents expect: income proof, employer statement, ID, references and a motivation letter in Dutch and English. Done once, used on every application.

steps.title: Hunt and apply

steps.title: Viewings, attended

steps.title: Negotiate, check, sign
steps.text: Rent, deposit, service costs, contract type and notice terms, all checked against Dutch law before you sign. Then keys, registration, and a person to call when the boiler breaks in week two.

checks.h2: Six things most internationals discover after signing.

items.title: The deposit cap
items.text: Dutch law caps the deposit at two months' rent. Agents still ask for three. We don't let them.

items.title: Registration
items.text: A landlord cannot forbid you from registering at the address (BRP). No registration means no BSN, no bank, no healthcare. We confirm it in writing before you pay.

items.title: The points system
items.text: Many Amsterdam apartments fall under rent regulation by the points system (WWS). If the asking rent is above the legal maximum, you have leverage. We run the check.

items.title: Service costs
items.text: "Rent €1,800 + €250 service costs" often hides unlawful charges. We separate what's legitimate from what's padding.

items.title: Contract type
items.text: Since 2024 the default rental contract in the Netherlands is indefinite. Fixed-term offers are the exception and have conditions. We check which one you're being handed.

items.title: Income rules
items.text: Starting a new job, freelancing, or paid in a non-euro currency? There's a right way to present each of these. We write it so it reads as safe to a Dutch landlord.

items.q: Isn't it illegal for agents to charge tenants in the Netherlands?
items.a: It's illegal for an agent to charge you when they also act for the landlord, which is what most "free" agencies do. An agent you hire, who works only for you, may charge you for the work. That is exactly what we are, and it's the only reason we can negotiate on your side.

items.q: How fast will I have an apartment?
items.a: With a complete dossier and applications inside the hour, most of our searches should close in two to six weeks depending on budget and move-in date. Nobody can promise a date in Amsterdam. Anyone who does is selling you something else.
It reserves one of the ten founding spots and locks the founding price for life. It's refundable any time before we start working, and it's deducted from your fee once we do.

items.q: What if you don't find anything?
items.a: Then we talk. The fee pays for a defined amount of work, and we'll be honest in the first call if your budget and timeline don't fit the market. We'd rather refund your deposit than take a search we don't believe in.
Because we can serve ten properly. BOOM Amsterdam is one local person and one portal, not a call centre. The cap is what makes the speed real.
